# web-mojo admin: dnsman Registrant Contact page

- **Kind**: feature
- **Date**: 2026-07-30
- **Requested by**: Ian
- **Project**: web-mojo
- **Depends on**: board item **951** (django-mojo — the per-group registrant-contact setting + REST). Do not build until 951 is `done`.

Apply rules: `nativemojo-board-conventions`.

## Description

Add a **Registrant Contact** page to the dnsman admin section so an operator can configure the ICANN contact that domain purchases require, without touching server settings. This is the **frontend half** of item 951.

The page edits two scopes: the **house** contact (used by every group that has no contact of its own) and a **per-group** contact. It also closes the dead end in the buy wizard — today a quote just fails with a raw 400 when no contact is configured.

## Context

`GET /api/dnsman/config` already reports `registrant_contact_configured`, and `dnsData.js` carries it in `DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES` — but nothing in the UI reads it. `DomainPurchaseWizard.js` never checks the flag, so an operator with no contact configured gets as far as pricing a domain and then hits an opaque quote error with no next step and no hint that the fix is a server setting.

The DNS section (`src/extensions/admin/dns/`) already has Domains, DNS Records, Certificates, Credentials, and Purchases pages, registered in `src/admin.js` and listed in the sidebar under System → DNS. This is a sixth entry in that group.

## Decisions (confirmed with Ian, 2026-07-30)

- **Scope**: per-group with a house fallback — the page edits both.
- **Permission**: `manage_dns`.
- **Placement**: a new page under System → DNS.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New page at `system/dns/registrant`, registered in `src/admin.js` with `permissions: ["manage_dns"]`, plus a sidebar entry in the existing DNS group.
- [ ] The page reads and writes the contact through 951's endpoints — it never touches `/api/settings` directly.
- [ ] A scope selector switches between the **house** contact and a **specific group's** contact. When a group has no contact of its own, the page says plainly that the house contact will be used — **without displaying the house contact's values** (it is the operator's personal PII; see 951's permission model).
- [ ] The form covers the ICANN field set: `FirstName`, `LastName`, `ContactType`, `OrganizationName` (optional), `AddressLine1`, `AddressLine2` (optional), `City`, `State`, `CountryCode`, `ZipCode`, `PhoneNumber`, `Email`.
- [ ] `ContactType` is a dropdown of the Route53 enum, and `CountryCode` a country picker rather than a free-text box.
- [ ] Client-side validation mirrors the server: every required field present; `State` required when the country is US or CA; `PhoneNumber` in ICANN format (`+1.5551234567`). The server stays the authority — a 400 is surfaced readably, not swallowed.
- [ ] Clearing a group's contact (reverting it to the house contact) is possible and asks for confirmation.
- [ ] Saving calls `registrar.resetCapabilities()` so `registrant_contact_configured` is re-fetched and the buy wizard unblocks without a reload.
- [ ] `DomainPurchaseWizard.js` checks `registrant_contact_configured` **before** search/quote and, when it is false, shows a clear message with a link to this page instead of letting the quote fail.
- [ ] `registrar.capabilities()` in `src/extensions/admin/models/Dns.js` stops assuming the answer is group-invariant — `registrant_contact_configured` now varies per group. Either key the cache by group or exclude that field from the shared cache. **Its docstring currently states the opposite and must be corrected.**
- [ ] Graceful degradation against an older backend without 951's endpoints (the page reports that the server does not support portal-managed contacts, rather than erroring) — matching how `DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES` already handles a missing `/config`.
- [ ] All rendered values are escaped — this form holds attacker-influenceable free text (names, addresses) and it renders back into the page.
- [ ] Unit tests under `test/unit/` in the style of the existing `Dns*.test.js` files: validation rules (required fields, US/CA state, phone format), scope switching, and the wizard's blocked state.
- [ ] Docs updated wherever the dnsman admin pages are described.

# Plan

## Objective

A **Registrant Contact** page at `system/dns/registrant` under System → DNS that reads and writes 951's `GET/POST /api/dnsman/registrant` for two scopes — the **house** contact and a **specific group's** — with client-side validation mirroring 951's `validate_contact()`, and no path by which a tenant-scoped admin can see the house contact's values. Alongside it: `registrar.capabilities()` stops being group-blind (951 makes `registrant_contact_configured` group-varying), and the buy-domain dead end gains a link to the fix instead of a bare "configure it on the server".

**Blocked**: item **951** is `planned`, not `done`. Do not start the build until it lands — its response shape (D5) and required-field set are this plan's contract.

## What scoping changed about the workspec

Two premises need correcting before the build reads them:

1. **The buy flow already checks the flag.** `DomainTablePage.onActionBuyDomain` (`src/extensions/admin/dns/DomainTablePage.js:139-143`) already refuses on `caps.registrant_contact_configured === false` with a readable message. The workspec's "an operator … gets as far as pricing a domain and then hits an opaque quote error" is not what ships today. The real remaining gaps are (a) the message names no fix ("configured on the server"), and (b) after 951 that gate reads the **house** answer while `takeQuote()` sends the **active group** — so a group with its own *incomplete* row passes the gate and fails at quote. That mismatch is created by 951 and is the substantive part of this AC.
2. **`purchase()`/`quote()` group resolution.** `DomainTablePage` and the wizard both resolve the group as `app.getActiveGroupId?.() || app.activeGroup?.id`. `getActiveGroupId` **does not exist anywhere in `src/`** — it is an optional-call that always returns undefined, so the live value is always `app.activeGroup?.id`. Don't add it; just mirror the existing expression so behaviour matches the rest of the section.

## Design decisions

### D1 — Two new files, no intermediate View

`registrantData.js` (pure, dependency-free) + `RegistrantContactPage.js` (a `Page` with one embedded `FormView` child). This is the `dnsData.js` + `DnsRecordsPage.js` shape, and it puts every rule that can be wrong in a module that is testable without a DOM — the property `dnsData.js`'s header claims and the reason the DNS surface is testable at all. A `RegistrantContactView` between them would buy nothing: unlike `DnsRecordsView` (mounted twice — page and `DomainView` section) this body has exactly one mount.

### D2 — House scope gates on the LITERAL `is_superuser`; the scope control is page-level, not a form field

**The predicate.** 951's global scope calls `require_platform_admin`, and that function (`django-mojo/mojo/apps/dnsman/rest/gates.py:42-50`) checks **`request.user.is_superuser` — the literal attribute** — plus a refusal for key-backed sessions. It does **not** consult `manage_dns`, `security`, or the `admin` wildcard. This repo already has the matching precedent, documented, for exactly this situation: `DomainTablePage.js:108-122` gates the Adopt button on `activeUser.get('is_superuser')` and explains why gating on `hasPermission('admin')` would "render a button that 403s for an admin-permissioned non-superuser". Same reasoning, same answer:

- `canEditHouse = !!this.getApp()?.activeUser?.get?.('is_superuser')`.
- **Superuser** → scope control rendered, default scope **house**.
- **Everyone else** (holds `manage_dns` through a member row, or globally but is not a superuser) → **no scope control**. Pinned to `app.activeGroup?.id`, with a line naming the group.

A browser session is never key-backed (`is_key_backed_session` is about `ApiKey.override_user`), so for this page the attribute check matches the server boundary exactly, not approximately.

**Do not probe the endpoint to discover the answer.** Issuing a no-group `GET /api/dnsman/registrant` on entry and reading the 403 would be authoritative — and would emit a `branch="dnsman.platform_admin.not_superuser"` denial, which `gates.py:38-41` documents as separated from ordinary tenant denials precisely because *"these are the ones worth alerting on."* Every non-superuser opening this page would raise a platform-boundary alert. A correct client-side predicate is available; use it.

**The control is not a FormView field.** `FormView`'s `showWhen` is driven from exactly one place — `handleFieldChange()` at `FormView.js:817` — and the `buttongroup` handler `onActionSelectButtonOption` (`FormView.js:1274-1313`) sets `this.data[field]` and emits directly, **never calling `handleFieldChange`**. A buttongroup therefore cannot drive a `showWhen` dependent: the picker renders hidden (`FormBuilder.js:874-886` bakes `display:none` at render) and nothing can unhide it — and `getFormData()` deletes keys inside hidden showWhen wrappers (`FormView.js:1798-1809`). Every existing `showWhen` controller in `src/` is a `select`/`toggle`/`switch`; there is no buttongroup precedent. So:

- The scope switch is a **page-level segmented control** in the page template with `data-action="scope-changed"`, handled by `onActionScopeChanged()` → `loadScope()`. No FormView involvement, no `showWhen`, no framework change.
- The group picker is its own one-field `FormView` (`type: 'collection'`, `Collection: GroupList`, `labelField: 'name'`, `valueField: 'id'` — the `Group.js:107` / `Push.js:74` pattern), **added when group scope is selected and removed when it is not**. Presence, not visibility.

Rejected: adding `handleFieldChange` to `onActionSelectButtonOption`. It would fix the class of bug, but it is a framework behaviour change affecting every buttongroup consumer and belongs in its own item, not smuggled into this one. **File it as a follow-up** — a documented option that silently does nothing is the same shape as `searchPlacement: 'dropdown'` (#494).

`?group=<id>` in the URL selects group scope for that id on entry (the `system/dns/records?domain=` precedent). A group id is not PII and this keeps a future GroupView deep-link cheap. The contact itself never touches the URL.

**Known limitation, note it in the docstring:** the group picker fetches `GroupList`, which the server gates on group VIEW_PERMS — orthogonal to `manage_dns`. A superuser passes; nothing else needs to. `?group=<id>` remains the escape hatch. Do not build a raw id-entry box for this.

### D3 — `capabilities()` gains an optional group key; `capabilities()` with no argument keeps its exact current meaning

Replace the two module-level cache variables in `src/extensions/admin/models/Dns.js:234-235` with two `Map`s keyed by `String(group ?? '')`. `capabilities()` → the house/global answer, byte-identical to today. There are **four** existing no-arg callers: `DnsRecordsView.js:163`, `DomainView.js:352`, `CertificateTablePage.js:111` — which want deployment-wide facts (`allowed_record_types`, `cert_renew_days`, `acme`) and are untouched — and `DomainTablePage.js:128`, which is the one Step 5 changes because it feeds a per-group decision. `capabilities(groupId)` is new. `resetCapabilities()` clears both maps entirely.

Rejected: excluding `registrant_contact_configured` from the cache. Callers read it synchronously off a stashed `this.caps`; making one field async-only would push a request into a click handler for every consumer, and the field would still be stale in `this.caps` — the shape the AC is trying to remove.

Request: `rest.GET('/api/dnsman/config', group ? { group } : {})`. `Rest.buildQueryString` drops null/undefined, so a null group is already safe, but pass the object conditionally anyway to keep the intent legible. A pre-951 backend ignores `?group=` and answers globally; a backend with no `/config` still falls back to `DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES`. Both degrade, neither errors.

**Correct the docstring at `Dns.js:243-247`**, which currently states the answer "does not vary per group" — after 951 that is false for `registrant_contact_configured` and is the reason this cache had to change.

### D4 — A new `registrantContact` client in `Dns.js`, and `group` is OMITTED (not null) for house scope

```js
export const registrantContact = {
    get(group)            { return rest.GET(`${BASE}/registrant`, group ? { group } : {}); },
    save(contact, group)  { return rest.POST(`${BASE}/registrant`, group ? { group, contact } : { contact }); },
    clear(group)          { return rest.POST(`${BASE}/registrant`, group ? { group, clear: true } : { clear: true }); }
};
```

The omission is load-bearing on the POST side. 951's Step 5 guard fires when `"group" in request.DATA` and `request.group` resolves to `None` — a JSON body carrying `group: null` satisfies `in` and would earn a readable-but-wrong 400 ("that group could not be resolved") on every house-scope save. GET is safe either way because `buildQueryString` drops nulls; POST is not, because the body is serialized as-is.

### D5 — Preserve contact keys the form does not edit

The form covers 12 fields. AWS's `ContactDetail` also carries `Fax` and `ExtraParams`, and 951's D4 explicitly keeps `ExtraParams` in the allow-list so ccTLD deployments keep working. `save_contact` **replaces the whole value** (`Setting.set(KEY, contact, …)`) — it does not merge. So a naive `POST { ...formValues }` silently destroys `ExtraParams` on the first edit of a contact created outside the portal.

`registrantData.buildContactPayload(raw, form)`:
- start from every key of `raw` that is **not** one of the 12 form fields (preserves `Fax`, `ExtraParams`, and anything a future AWS shape adds);
- overlay the 12 form fields, **omitting any whose trimmed value is `''`**.

Omitting blanks is what makes *clearing* an optional field work (the key is simply absent from the replacing value) and avoids sending `OrganizationName: ""` to Route53. Required fields can never be blank past validation, so the omission never strips one.

**`raw` is scope-bound, and this is a hard invariant — violating it leaks the operator's PII into a tenant's row.** `ExtraParams` is where AWS carries `BIRTH_DATE_IN_YYYY_MM_DD`, `ES_IDENTIFICATION`, `CA_LEGAL_TYPE` — the operator's date of birth and national ID — and none of it is rendered on screen, so nothing on the page would show a superuser that it was being carried. The failure sequence: open the page (defaults to house scope, `raw` = the operator's contact) → switch to a tenant group with no row (form renders empty per D7) → fill in the tenant's contact and save → `buildContactPayload` bases the payload on the **house** `Fax` + `ExtraParams` → `save_contact` replaces group 42's whole value with it → any `manage_dns` holder on group 42 reads it back through 951's own-row GET, fully authorized. Every server-side control 951 built stays intact and irrelevant; the leak is client-manufactured, and 951's test 3 ("house values appear nowhere in the body") still passes.

So the page holds `this._raw`, and:
- it is **cleared to `null` on every scope change**, before the new load is issued;
- it is set **only** from a successful load of the *current* scope, and **only when `source === 'database'`** — `source: 'none'` and any `inherited` payload leave it `null`;
- it is cleared on any failed or refused load;
- `buildContactPayload(null, form)` bases on `{}`.

The preserved-keys note renders from the current scope's `_raw` only — as an unbound `raw` it would announce the *house's* `ExtraParams` inside a tenant-scoped view.

When `_raw` carries preserved keys, render a read-only note naming them: *"This contact also carries registrar parameters not editable here (ExtraParams). They are preserved when you save."* Silent preservation of an invisible field is how the next person deletes it by hand.

### D6 — Validation is a pure function, not HTML5 validity

`registrantData.validateContact(contact)` → array of `{ field, message }`, empty when valid. Mirrors 951 D4:

- required: `FirstName`, `LastName`, `ContactType`, `AddressLine1`, `City`, `CountryCode`, `ZipCode`, `PhoneNumber`, `Email`; plus `State` when `CountryCode` ∈ `{US, CA}` (`STATE_REQUIRED_COUNTRIES`);
- `ContactType` ∈ `PERSON | COMPANY | ASSOCIATION | PUBLIC_BODY | RESELLER`;
- `PhoneNumber` matches `/^\+\d{1,3}\.\d{4,15}$/`;
- `CountryCode` matches `/^[A-Z]{2}$/`;
- empty/whitespace-only counts as missing (`String(v).trim()`), matching the server.

`FormView.validate()` is native `checkValidity()` only, which cannot express "required when the country is US or CA" — and hiding `State` via `showWhen` would be wrong twice over (AWS accepts `State` for other countries, and hiding a filled field invites dropping its value). So `State` is always visible and never carries `required`; the conditional rule lives in `validateContact()`. `required: true` is still set on the nine unconditionally-required fields for browser/a11y semantics, but **`formView.validate()` is never called** — the page's Save handler runs `validateContact()` and is the only gate.

Problems render as an inline list above the buttons, and each named field gets `.is-invalid` via `form.elements[field]`.

**The server stays the authority.** The required set is mirrored from 951's `REQUIRED_CONTACT_FIELDS` and cannot be read at runtime — there is no schema endpoint. The build session must diff this list against 951 as shipped. A mismatch in the permissive direction is absorbed by rendering the server's 400 inline (951 D4 names the field); a mismatch in the restrictive direction blocks a save the server would accept, so **if in doubt, drop the client check and let the server answer**.

### D7 — Inherited scope shows a statement, never the house values

951's GET answers a group with no row as `{contact: null, source: "none", inherited: true, effective_configured: true, problems: []}`. The page renders an **empty form** plus a banner. The page never issues a house-scope GET while in group scope, and never falls back to one on a 403. `problems` is scope-own-only per 951, so an `inherited` scope renders no problems list at all.

**Word the banner for the parent chain, not just the house.** `Setting.resolve()` walks the **parent group chain** before falling back to the global row (951, Edge cases), so a child group with no row of its own inherits its *parent's* contact, not necessarily the house one — and 951's response says `inherited: true` without naming the source (correctly: the values are not returned either way). So: *"This group has no contact of its own — domain purchases for it use the contact inherited from its parent group, or the house contact. Those details are not shown here."* Asserting "the house contact" would be a confident, wrong statement about whose name ends up on the registration.

`source: "settings_file"` (global scope only) renders the deploy-file note the geofence editor already uses (`GeofenceRulesView.js:61-67`): saving creates a DB row that shadows the file; clearing reverts to the file, not to "unconfigured".

### D8 — Degradation and failure surfaces

- **Pre-951 backend** → GET returns 404. Detect `resp.status === 404` (the `GeofencingPage.js:115-117` precedent; `Rest.processResponseInterceptors` puts the HTTP status on the response) and render an explanatory panel naming `DNSMAN_REGISTRANT_CONTACT` as the deployment-settings alternative. **Do not name a django-mojo version** unless 951's close-out records one — a wrong version number is worse than none.
- **403 on a house-scope load** → **demote to group scope** (pin to `app.activeGroup?.id`, drop the scope control, note it inline) rather than dead-ending. D2's predicate matches the server boundary, so this should not fire — but a plan that guesses a permission must not strand the user when the guess is wrong, and there is a correct thing to show. Never fall back to a *read* of another scope.
- **403 on a group-scope load or save** → the server's message inline; no fallback read, no partial render.
- **400 on save** → `resp.data.error` inline, form state kept so the user can fix and retry.
- **Network failure** → the generic message; nothing is assumed saved.

### D9 — `resetCapabilities()` after save **and** after clear

The AC names save. Clearing a group's contact also changes its effective answer (from its own row to the house fallback, which may be unconfigured), so both paths reset. With D3's maps, one `resetCapabilities()` drops every scope's entry, which is correct — a house-contact save changes the effective answer of every group without a row.

### D10 — Scope: contact form only, with one exception

Open question 1 → **no purchase/price-cap summary panel**; the workspec puts that out of scope. The single exception: when `caps.purchase_enabled === false`, one line stating that purchasing is disabled deployment-wide so a configured contact will not enable buying. Without it this page becomes the next dead end — a user configures a contact, returns to Domains, and gets refused by the *other* gate at `DomainTablePage.js:133-137`. **Flagged for Ian to overturn** if he wants the page kept strictly to the form.

### D11 — Escaping

Contact values reach the DOM only through `FormView` (`FormBuilder.renderInputField` → `value="{{fieldValue}}"`, Mustache-escaped). Everything the page renders itself — group name, server `error`/`problems` strings, preserved-key names — goes through `MOJOUtils.escapeHtml`, matching every other file in this directory. Nothing in this page uses `{{{ }}}` for server-sourced data.

## Implementation steps

**Step 0 — baseline.** `npm test` before the first edit; record total/passed/failed on the item's activity trail (`.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`). Red baseline → stop and report.

**Step 1 — `src/extensions/admin/dns/registrantData.js`** (new, dependency-free, aggregate `export default` like `dnsData.js`):
- `CONTACT_FIELDS` (the 12 editable), `PRESERVED_FIELDS` note, `CONTACT_TYPES`, `CONTACT_TYPE_OPTIONS`, `REQUIRED_FIELDS`, `STATE_REQUIRED_COUNTRIES = ['US','CA']`, `PHONE_RE`, `COUNTRY_CODE_RE`.
- `validateContact(contact)` → `[{field, message}]` (D6).
- `buildContactPayload(raw, form)` (D5).
- `contactToForm(contact)` → the 12 keys as strings, `''` for absent.
- `buildContactFields()` → the `FormView` field array: `ContactType` a `select` over `CONTACT_TYPE_OPTIONS`; `CountryCode` a `select` over `COUNTRIES` from `@ext/admin/security/geofence/GeofenceRuleForm.js` (ISO2 → name, derived from `@ext/map/countryCentroids.js` — the framework's only country-name source, already used by the geofence editor); `Email` type `email`; `PhoneNumber` type `text` with `placeholder: '+1.5551234567'` and `attributes: { pattern: '^\\+\\d{1,3}\\.\\d{4,15}$' }`; two-column layout via `columns`.
  - *Import note*: this makes `registrantData.js` non-dependency-free unless `COUNTRIES` is imported by the **page** instead. Keep `registrantData.js` pure — `buildContactFields(countryOptions)` takes the list as an argument (the `dnsData.js` "helpers take `caps` as an argument" convention), and `RegistrantContactPage.js` passes `COUNTRIES` in.

**Step 2 — `src/extensions/admin/models/Dns.js`**: group-keyed capability maps + `capabilities(group)` + `resetCapabilities()` (D3); corrected docstring at :243-247; new `registrantContact` client (D4); add `registrantContact` to both the named exports and the aggregate default.

**Step 3 — `src/extensions/admin/dns/RegistrantContactPage.js`** (new `Page`, route `system/dns/registrant`):
- Template: `container-lg py-3`, title row, a **page-level segmented scope control** rendered only for a superuser (plain buttons with `data-action="scope-changed" data-scope="house|group"` — *not* a FormView field, D2), `data-container="group-picker"` for the one-field group `FormView`, status/banner region, contact card (`data-container="contact-form"`), Save / Discard / *Clear this group's contact* buttons + inline status span — the `GeofenceRulesView` button row shape.
- `onInit()` computes `canEditHouse` from the literal `is_superuser` (D2). Neither form is built here — both depend on scope, which is resolved on entry.
- `onEnter()`: `await super.onEnter()` **then** fire the load without awaiting; stash into `_pending` and apply from `onAfterMount()` on the first visit (WM-023 — both halves).
- `onActionScopeChanged()`: dirty-check → confirm → set `this.scope`, **clear `this._raw` to `null`** (D5), add/remove the group-picker `FormView`, `loadScope()`.
- `loadScope()`: `registrantContact.get(groupId)` → `applyPayload()`; sets `unsupported` on 404, demotes to group scope on a house-scope 403, `forbidden` on a group-scope 403 (D8). Clears `_raw` before issuing.
- `applyPayload()`: set `this._raw` per D5's invariant (only on `source === 'database'` for the *current* scope, else `null`), rebuild the contact `FormView` (`removeChild` → `render()` → `addChild` → `await child.render()` — post-first-render children need the explicit render, `views.md`), set the inherited / deploy-file / problems banners, set the effective-configured chip.
- `onActionSaveContact()`: `await this.contactForm.getFormData()` (**it is `async` — `FormView.js:1702`**) → `buildContactPayload(this._raw, form)` → `validateContact` → on problems, render inline and stop → else `registrantContact.save()` → on success `registrar.resetCapabilities()`, toast, reload the scope → on failure render `resp.data.error` inline.
- `onActionClearContact()`: `Modal.confirm(...)` (`Modal.confirm(message, title, {confirmText, confirmClass})` → boolean) naming what reverting means, then `registrantContact.clear(groupId)` → `resetCapabilities()` → reload. Group scope only; never offered for house scope (clearing the house contact blocks purchasing for every group without a row — out of scope for this item, and a `Modal.confirm` is not the right gate for it).
- No `localStorage`, no logging of contact values, no contact in the URL.

**Step 4 — `src/admin.js`**: export `RegistrantContactPage` in the DNS block (~:82-98); `import RegistrantContactPageClass` beside the other DNS page imports (~:230-233); `app.registerPage('system/dns/registrant', RegistrantContactPageClass, {permissions: ["manage_dns"]})` after the purchases line (~:271); sidebar entry after Purchases: `{ text: 'Registrant Contact', route: '?page=system/dns/registrant', icon: 'bi-person-vcard', permissions: ["manage_dns"] }` (icon verified present in bootstrap-icons 1.11.3 and already used at `UserProfileView.js:74`). The DNS group header stays `["view_dns","manage_dns"]`; a stricter child inside a looser group is the existing pattern.

**Step 5 — `src/extensions/admin/dns/DomainTablePage.js`**: in `onActionBuyDomain`, resolve `const group = app?.activeGroup?.id` first, `const caps = await registrar.capabilities(group)` (cached; the second call is free), gate on that instead of the `onEnter`-stashed global `this.caps`, and replace the contact message with one that offers the fix — a `Modal.confirm` whose confirm button navigates to `?page=system/dns/registrant`, shown only when the viewer holds `manage_dns` (otherwise the current text, minus "on the server"). **Pass that same group-scoped `caps` object to the wizard**, not `this.caps`. Keep `this.caps` (the no-arg, deployment-wide answer) for `purchase_enabled` only.

**Step 6 — `src/extensions/admin/dns/DomainPurchaseWizard.js`**: a `blocked` branch in `renderBody()` when `this.caps.registrant_contact_configured === false`, plus an early return in `runSearch()`.

This is only defense in depth **because Step 5 hands it group-scoped caps**. The wizard has no independent source: `this.caps = options.caps` (`DomainPurchaseWizard.js:50`), and today that comes from `DomainTablePage.js:128`'s no-arg `capabilities()` — the *house* answer. Left as-is, the wizard's new branch would evaluate `true === false` for precisely the case this item exists to fix (a group with its own invalid row, house answer `true`), i.e. it would re-implement the same wrong-scope read in a second place rather than defend against it. The two changes are one change; do not land Step 6 without Step 5's `caps` hand-off.

**Step 7 — tests** (see below).

**Step 8 — docs + changelog + memory** (see below).

## Edge cases and error handling

- **`group: null` in a POST body** → 951's group-resolution guard 400s. Omit the key (D4). This is the single most likely implementation slip in the item.
- **A group with its own *invalid* row** → `effective_configured: false` for that group while the house answer is `true`. The Step 5 gate must read the group's answer or it opens a wizard that cannot quote.
- **Scope switched mid-edit** → unsaved edits are discarded. Confirm before switching when the form is dirty (`FormView` tracks originals; a plain `Modal.confirm` on scope change when `getFormData()` differs from the loaded contact is enough).
- **`ExtraParams` / `Fax` present** → preserved and named, never silently dropped (D5).
- **Clearing an already-empty group scope** → the button is not rendered when `source === 'none'`; there is nothing to clear.
- **Clearing the global scope with a deploy-file value present** → reverts to the file, not to unconfigured. Out of scope: the house clear control is not built (D3/Step 3).
- **`problems` non-empty on load** → warning banner: saved but incomplete, purchases refused until fixed. Never shown for an inherited scope.
- **Group picker empty** (no group-list permission) → the picker's own empty state plus the `?group=` note (D2).
- **Switching house → group, then saving** → `_raw` must be `null`, or the house `Fax`/`ExtraParams` are written into the tenant's row (D5). This is the sharpest failure mode in the item; it has a named test.
- **Double-click Save** → disable the button for the duration of the request, as the wizard does for purchase.
- **404 vs proxy 404** → treated as unsupported. Accepted; the same assumption `GeofencingPage` already ships.

## Testing plan

New `test/unit/RegistrantContact.test.js` — pure `registrantData` (the `DnsData.test.js` shape, `moduleLoader.loadModuleFromFile`):
- every required field missing → named in `problems`; whitespace-only counts as missing;
- `State` required for `US` and `CA`, optional for `GB`, and **accepted** (not stripped) for `GB`;
- `ContactType` outside the enum rejected; each of the five accepted;
- `PhoneNumber`: `+1.5551234567` valid; `555-123-4567`, `+15551234567`, `+1.555` rejected;
- `CountryCode`: `US` valid, `usa` / `U1` rejected;
- `buildContactPayload` preserves `ExtraParams` and `Fax`, omits blank optionals, and **drops a cleared** `OrganizationName` rather than restoring it from `raw`;
- **`buildContactPayload(null, form)` carries no `ExtraParams` and no `Fax`** — the base is `{}`. This is the cross-scope PII regression (D5); write it as a named test, not an incidental assertion;
- `contactToForm` round-trips through `buildContactPayload` for a well-formed contact.

New `test/unit/RegistrantContactPage.test.js` — construction/handler-driven (WM-026), with `stripComments` + `methodBody` helpers copied from `DnsViews.test.js` / `DomainPurchaseWizard.test.js` (both files document in prose what they refuse to do, and this one will too):
- group scope with `contact: null, inherited: true` sets the inherited banner and leaves the form empty — and no house-scope GET is issued;
- `problems` are not rendered when `inherited` is true;
- a 404 response sets the unsupported state, not an empty form;
- save and clear both call `registrar.resetCapabilities()`;
- house scope sends **no `group` key** in the POST body (assert on the built body object, not the source text);
- **`onActionScopeChanged` clears `_raw`**, and a house→group switch followed by a save posts a body with no `Fax`/`ExtraParams` — the D5 leak, driven through the page's own handlers rather than the pure helper;
- `canEditHouse` reads the literal `is_superuser`, not `hasPermission` — assert an `activeUser` stub with `permissions: {admin: true}` and `is_superuser` falsy gets **no** scope control (the `DomainTablePage` Adopt-button invariant, one directory over);
- source assertion: no `localStorage`, and the contact never reaches `app.navigate`/the URL.
- *Test-infra*: add `{ test: /dns\/registrantData(\.js)?$/, name: 'registrantData' }` to `importPathToGlobal` in `test/utils/simple-module-loader.js` (the `dnsData` rule immediately above it is the precedent and carries the same comment), and register the page in the loader if needed. Set `global.registrantData` before the load, then **capture-then-delete** — a lingering global leaks into later files (WM-026).

Extend `test/unit/DnsRecordList.test.js`'s recipe into a new `test/unit/DnsCapabilities.test.js`: `global.Rest = { GET: jest.fn() }` before `loadModuleFromFile(..., 'Dns')`, then assert `capabilities()` and `capabilities(7)` issue **two** requests, that each is served from cache on a second call, that `capabilities(7)` sends `{group: 7}` and `capabilities()` sends `{}`, and that `resetCapabilities()` clears both. Use a **distinct cache name** for the loaded module — `loadModuleFromFile` caches by name and a cache hit does not re-run the transform, so reusing `'Dns'` after `DnsRecordList.test.js` would silently return the earlier instance.

Extend `test/unit/DomainPurchaseWizard.test.js`: `renderBody()` returns the blocked state and `runSearch()` no-ops when `caps.registrant_contact_configured === false`.

Run `npm run test:unit` while iterating; `npm test` + `npm run lint` (baseline 0 errors) before closing.

## Documentation plan

- `docs/web-mojo/extensions/Admin.md` — three places: the DNS bullet at **:41** (add the Registrant Contact page and the house/per-group model), the route inventory at **:144** (add `system/dns/registrant`), and the permissions section at **:290** (this page is `manage_dns` only — `view_dns` does not reach it — and the house scope additionally needs platform-admin rights; it is the fourth "stricter than it looks" surface in that paragraph).
- `CHANGELOG.md` — an `### Admin · …` entry under `## Unreleased`: the new page, the group-keyed capability cache and why (951 made the flag group-varying), and the buy-domain gate now reading the group's answer.
- `memory.md` — a Key Decisions bullet covering the four things that would otherwise be re-derived: house scope gates on the **literal `is_superuser`** because `require_platform_admin` does (`gates.py:47`), matching the Adopt-button precedent; `group` **omitted, not null**, in the POST body; `buildContactPayload`'s base is **scope-bound** or it writes house PII into a tenant row; `capabilities()` with no argument still means "deployment-wide".
- No `examples/portal/` entry: admin extension pages are not covered by the examples portal (no dnsman route exists there today), and no public component or option changed.

### Challenge

An independent red-team pass reviewed this plan against the code, and every objection was re-verified in this session before being dispositioned.

- **The scope selector was mechanically inoperative** — *amended*, and the strongest objection. D2 originally drove a `showWhen` group picker from a `buttongroup`. `_updateShowWhen` has exactly one caller — `handleFieldChange` at `FormView.js:817` — and `onActionSelectButtonOption` (`FormView.js:1274-1313`) sets `this.data[field]` and emits without ever calling it. The picker would render `display:none` (`FormBuilder.js:874-886`) and nothing could unhide it; `getFormData()` also drops keys inside hidden showWhen wrappers (`FormView.js:1798-1809`). Every `showWhen` controller that exists in `src/` is a `select`/`toggle`/`switch`. Verified directly. The scope control is now a page-level `data-action` segmented control and the picker is added/removed rather than shown/hidden. The framework bug is filed as a follow-up rather than fixed inline.

- **`buildContactPayload` could write the operator's PII into a tenant's row** — *amended*, and the most serious defect by consequence. D5's `raw` was unbound to scope: open the page (house scope, `raw` = operator's contact incl. `Fax` and `ExtraParams`, neither rendered) → switch to a tenant group with no row → fill and save → the payload is based on the house extras and `save_contact` replaces the group's whole value. `ExtraParams` is where AWS carries `BIRTH_DATE_IN_YYYY_MM_DD` and `ES_IDENTIFICATION`. Every server control in 951 stays intact and irrelevant — the leak is client-manufactured, and 951's "house values appear nowhere in the body" test still passes. `_raw` is now scope-bound with an explicit invariant, cleared on every scope change and set only from a `source: "database"` load of the current scope, with two named tests.

- **The wizard's blocked branch would have read the house answer** — *amended*. `DomainPurchaseWizard.this.caps = options.caps` (`:50`), fed from `DomainTablePage.js:128`'s no-arg `capabilities()`. As drafted, Step 6 re-implemented the wrong-scope read it was meant to defend against, and would evaluate `true === false` for exactly the invalid-group-row case this item exists to fix. Step 5 now hands the wizard the group-scoped caps and the two steps are marked as one change. The related count slip is fixed too: `capabilities()` has **four** no-arg callers, not three, and the omitted one was the one that matters.

- **D2's permission predicate was wrong, but not in the direction proposed** — *amended*. The challenger correctly attacked the `sys.`-prefix inference (`sys.manage_dns` also passes on the `admin` wildcard and on the `security` category, so it is broader than `require_platform_admin`) and proposed probing the endpoint and reading the 403. Reading `django-mojo/mojo/apps/dnsman/rest/gates.py` settles both halves: `require_platform_admin` checks **`request.user.is_superuser`, the literal attribute** (`:47`), so the correct client predicate is the literal attribute — the precedent already documented one directory over for the Adopt button (`DomainTablePage.js:108-122`). And the proposed probe is *refuted*: `gates.py:38-41` states these denials carry a separate incident branch because "these are the ones worth alerting on", so probing would fire a platform-boundary alert for every non-superuser who opens the page. Predicate corrected; probe rejected with the reason recorded. D8 additionally demotes a house-scope 403 to group scope rather than dead-ending, so a wrong guess strands nobody.

- **The inherited banner asserted the wrong source** — *amended*, self-found while checking the above. `Setting.resolve()` walks the **parent group chain** before the global row (951, Edge cases), so a child group inherits its parent's contact, not necessarily the house one. The banner no longer claims which.

- **`getFormData()` is `async`** (`FormView.js:1702`) — *amended* into Step 3.

- **Verified and left standing:** `Rest.buildQueryString` drops null/undefined so D4's GET/POST asymmetry argument holds (`Rest.js:236-251`); `getActiveGroupId` genuinely does not exist in `src/` and is only ever called optionally; `DomainTablePage.js:139-143` really does already gate on `registrant_contact_configured`, so the workspec's framing of the dead end was wrong; the 404 precedent (`GeofencingPage.js:115-117`); `Modal.confirm`'s signature (`Modal.js:485`); D11's escaping claim (`FormBuilder.js:76,87,106` use double-brace `value="{{fieldValue}}"`); and the module-loader mechanics the test plan depends on, including the name-keyed cache that motivates the distinct-cache-name warning (`simple-module-loader.js:98-123, 595-609`).

## Follow-ups to file (not built here)

- **`buttongroup` cannot drive `showWhen`.** `onActionSelectButtonOption` (`FormView.js:1274-1313`) never calls `handleFieldChange`, which is `_updateShowWhen`'s only caller (`:817`); it also emits `field:changed` where the rest of the form emits `field:change`. A documented option that silently does nothing — the same shape as `searchPlacement: 'dropdown'` (#494), and the fix should be fail-safe in the same way. Found while scoping this item; routed around here (D2) rather than fixed.
